Describe the techniques for gathering information when creating simple messages.

- Consider the audience's perspective. Put yourself in the audience's position: what are these people thinking, feeling, or planning? What information do they need in order to move forward? What questions would they have about your topic? If you are initiating a conversation in a social media context, what information will stimulate discussion in your target communities?
- Listen to the community. For almost any subject related to business these days, chances are there is a community of customers, product enthusiasts, or other people linked through social media who engage in online discussions. Find them and listen to what they have to say.
- Read reports and other company documents. Annual reports, financial statements, news releases, blogs and microblogs by industry experts, marketing reports, and customer surveys are just a few of the many potential sources of information. Find out whether your company has a knowledge-management system, a database that collects the experiences and insights of employees throughout the organization.
- Talk with supervisors, colleagues, or customers. Fellow workers and customers may have information you need, or they may have insights into the needs of your target audience.
- Ask your audience for input. If you're unsure what audience members need from your message, ask them if at all possible. Admitting you don't know but want to meet their needs will impress an audience more than guessing and getting it wrong.

- Is the information accurate and complete? Inaccuracies and missing information can cause a host of problems, from embarrassment and lost productivity to serious safety and legal issues. Be sure to review any mathematical or financial calculations. Check all dates and schedules. Examine your own assumptions and conclusions to be certain they are valid.
- Is the information ethical? By working hard to ensure the accuracy of the information you gather, you'll also avoid many ethical problems in your messages. However, messages can also be unethical if important information is omitted or obscured.
- Is the information pertinent? Some points will be more important to your audience than others. Focusing on the information that concerns your audience the most can increase your chances of sending an effective message.

Discuss the advantages of visual messages in cross-cultural communication.

Many business communicators are discovering the power of messages in which the visual element is dominant and supported by small amounts of text. Messages that combine powerful visuals with supporting text can be effective for a number of reasons. Today's audiences are pressed for time and bombarded with messages, so anything that communicates quickly is welcome. Visuals are also effective at describing complex ideas and processes because they can reduce the work required for an audience to identify the parts and relationships that make up the whole. Also, in a multilingual business world, diagrams, symbols, and other images can lower communication barriers by requiring less language processing. Finally, visual images can be easier to remember than purely textual descriptions or explanations.

Briefly describe at least four factors to consider in choosing a medium for your message.

In considering which medium to use for your message, it is important to consider: 1. Media richness-the medium's ability to utilize more than one informational cue, facilitate feedback, and establish personal focus; 2. Message formality, including your audience's expectations for style and tone; 3. Media limitations; 4. Sender intentions-your choice of medium will influence how the audience perceives your intentions; 5. Urgency and cost; and 6. Audience preferences, paying close attention to any cultural variations.

Your organization decides to switch its top-down decision-making structure with a participatory approach, in which all employees have a say in decision-making. Draft the message using first the direct and then the indirect approach. Describe the type of audience for each approach and explain why that particular approach is necessary.

The direct approach can be used when you know your audience will be receptive to your message. This starts with the main idea (such as a recommendation, conclusion, or request) and follows that with supporting evidence. Employees who had previously no say in decision-making will be receptive to the new approach and may be reached through the direct approach.

The indirect approach can be used when the audience will be skeptical about or even resistant to the message. It generally starts with the evidence first and build a case before presenting the main idea. Note that taking the indirect approach does not mean avoiding tough issues or talking around in circles. It simply means building up to the main idea in a careful and logical way. The indirect approach may be used to address the higher levels of the organization, who, under the previous structure, made most of the decisions.

School authorities are about to introduce tough new security measures to prevent crime on campus. Students will have to carry identification at all times, and some activities will be restricted. Draft a message explaining the new rules using either the direct or indirect approach. Explain which approach the school should use to communicate with students and why.

Students may perceive the new security measures negatively, viewing them as restrictions on their freedom. The best approach to communicate the new measures in this case is the indirect approach. This approach is used when the audience is skeptical about or even resistant to the message. With the indirect approach, the message starts with the evidence first, and a case is built before presenting the main idea.

Indirect approach: "Crime on campus has escalated drastically over the past two months. Crimes against students have tripled compared to last year and show no signs of abating. To ensure the safety of students and faculty, the school is instituting new rules and heightened security measures. Effective February 1, 2011, students are required to carry identification at all times and comply with the instructions of the security guards on campus. All meetings of groups and associations will conclude by 9:00 p.m. Please cooperate with the security team to ensure your safety."

Students may react positively to the message as it makes the campus safer. If this is the likely reaction, the university authorities can use the direct approach, which starts with the main idea (such as a recommendation, conclusion, or request) and follows it with supporting evidence.

Direct approach: "Effective February 1, 2011, all students will be required to carry school identification at all times. All meetings of groups and associations on campus will conclude by 9:00 p.m., and students are requested to comply with the instructions of campus security. These measures have been taken in view of the increasing number of crimes on campus. Please cooperate with the security team to ensure your safety."
Using an example, explain the advantages of the storytelling method in business communications.

Stories can be an effective way to organize messages in a surprising number of business communication scenarios, from recruiting and training employees to enticing investors and customers. Career-related stories, such as how someone sought and found the opportunity to work on projects he or she is passionate about, can entice skilled employees to consider joining a firm. Entrepreneurs use stories to help investors see how their new ideas have the potential to affect people lives (and therefore generate lots of sales). Stories can be cautionary tales as well, dramatizing the consequences of career blunders, ethical mistakes, and strategic missteps.

A key reason storytelling can be so effective is that stories help readers and listeners imagine themselves living through the experience of the person in the story. As a result, people tend to remember and respond to the message in ways that can be difficult to achieve with other forms of communication. In addition, stories can demonstrate cause-and-effect relationships in a compelling fashion.
Discuss the benefits of using storytelling techniques in business communications.

Storytelling is an extremely common device and is very familiar to us both as communicators and as audiences. Storytelling is relatively natural to do and it is easy to adapt the classic three-part story narrative to most business situations. One of the reasons that storytelling is so effective is that listeners can imagine themselves living through the experience of the person in the story, thus increasing retention.
Discuss what haptic technologies are and how they are important in business.

Haptic communication, or haptics, is the study of touch in a communication context. Touch is a vital aspect of human-to-human and human-to-machine interaction, but it is missing from most forms of digital communication. You can't give someone a hearty handshake over email or feel the vibration patterns of a machine while viewing it over a video link. The technology has exciting potential in such diverse areas as training, online retailing, and increasing the number of devices that are usable by people with limited vision.

To make sure that you use email effectively, efficiently, and safely, what guidelines should you follow? List at least FIVE.

Any five of the following are acceptable:

  • Do not send large files (including large attachments) without prior notice.
  • Proofread every message.
  • Respect other people's electronic space by sending messages only when necessary.
  • Respond to messages promptly.
  • Avoid overusing the label "urgent."
  • Be careful about using the "reply all" button.
  • Remember that email is not always private.
  • Use the "Save as Draft" feature to give yourself time to consider the style and tone of important messages.
  • Many people read their emails on smartphones, so keep messages brief and to the point.
  • Use complete sentences with proper punctuation and spelling.
